assessment: The overarching hypothesis is that cadherin adhesion molecules specify the code that enables the premotor brainstem breathing circuits to innervate the phrenic motor neurons that control the primary breathing muscle, the diaphragm. This concept is important for understanding how the breathing control circuit is established and in general, how motor circuitry is developed. This is an extremely thorough investigation of the role of cadherins in generating a functional motor circuit.
